data.short_meaning: God of Mountains, Lord of Auspiciousness
data.long_meaning: Shara means mountain and Ankir means lord of auspiciousness, making Sharankir the god of mountains and the lord of auspiciousness. In Hindu mythology, he is considered to be a form of Lord Shiva. The name Sharankir carries the meaning “God of Mountains, Lord of Auspiciousness” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Sharankir usually hope their child will grow to embody god of mountains, lord of auspiciousness and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength, wisdom, and protection. It is believed that those named Sharankir are blessed with these qualities and are able to overcome challenges and obstacles in their lives.
data.etymology: Sharankir belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God of Mountains, Lord of Auspiciousness.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Sharankir total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: Sharankir is a name that holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism. It is believed that mountains are sacred places and are often considered to be the abode of various deities. Sharankir, being the lord of mountains, holds a special place in Hindu mythology. In many temples and pilgrimages, shrines are dedicated to Sharankir as a manifestation of Lord Shiva, showcasing the importance of nature and spirituality in Hindu culture.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Sharankir represents the connection between the divine and the physical world. The mountains, as symbols of stability, strength, and resilience, are seen as a reflection of the divine. Sharankir, as the lord of mountains, is believed to bestow blessings of stability, strength, and prosperity upon his devotees. He is often invoked during auspicious occasions and for the fulfillment of desires, highlighting the idea that the divine can be accessed through nature and through the practices of devotion and spirituality.
